Enforces the v1 rule that actor identity is never accepted from the request
body: any present field (for example ``created_by``) fails validation with
a 422 ``request_validation_failed`` envelope.

LogQueryRequestModel.title: LogQueryRequestModel

OperationAccepted.description:
The 202 body a route returns after enqueuing a durable operation.

Carries only ``accepted=True`` and the new ``operation_id`` so a caller can
follow the operation through the ``/api/v1/operations`` read surface without
ever echoing a redacted payload or an actor identity back to the wire.
OperationAccepted.title: OperationAccepted

OperationKind.description: The stable kind vocabulary for durable operations.
OperationKind.title: OperationKind

OperationView.description:
The client-facing representation of an operation.

Omits the redacted ``request_payload`` and the internal claim/identity
columns so private request text and the actor identity never reach a client.
OperationView.title: OperationView

Principal.description:
An authenticated actor for the duration of one request.

``allowed_target_ids`` is ``None`` when the principal is allowed to address
every target; otherwise the explicit allow-list is the only set of targets
the principal may reference.  The model is frozen and rejects unknown
fields so identity can never be smuggled through a request body.
Principal.title: Principal

PrincipalScope.description: Coarse-grained capability buckets granted to a principal.
PrincipalScope.title: PrincipalScope

ResumeInvestigationRequest.description: Body naming the agent run to resume.
ResumeInvestigationRequest.title: ResumeInvestigationRequest

SessionCreated.description:
Response model for ``POST /api/v1/auth/session``.

The CSRF token is returned in the body because browser-based clients need
it to authenticate cookie sessions on later mutations; it is also recoverable
from the signed cookie by any client that knows the signing key, but the
response is the supported channel.
SessionCreated.title: SessionCreated

StartInvestigationRequest.description: Body to start (or resume) an investigation with a parent-run scope.
StartInvestigationRequest.title: StartInvestigationRequest

TargetCreate.description:
Body for ``POST /api/v1/targets``.

``authentication_ref`` is an SSH identity reference (for example an
``ssh-agent:<user>@<host>`` URI or the name of a named profile) stored
server-side and never echoed back to a client.  ``optional_source_path`` is
product-local display metadata and never participates in path authorization.
TargetCreate.title: TargetCreate

TargetPatch.description:
Body for ``PATCH /api/v1/targets/{id}`` (optimistic concurrency).

``expected_version`` must match the current facade ``version`` or the patch
fails with a stable ``resource_conflict`` (409).  Only the fields a caller
sets are applied; everything else (including services and scope on the
authoritative record) is preserved.
TargetPatch.title: TargetPatch

TargetServiceView.description:
One service exposed through ``GET /api/v1/targets/{id}/services``.

Resolved from the authoritative ProjectRegistry record, never duplicated in
the facade table.
TargetServiceView.title: TargetServiceView

TargetView.description:
The product-facing representation of a target.

``authentication_configured`` and ``authentication_hint`` are the only
traces of the server-side ``authentication_ref``; the full reference is
never serialized.
TargetView.title: TargetView

Body for ``POST /api/v1/changesets/{id}/rollback``.

``approval_id`` is the single-use approval covering a service-interrupting
rollback; it is carried into the durable operation payload so the rollback
handler can consume it exactly once.

post.description: End the browser session by clearing the session cookie.

Exchange a bearer token for a signed ``incidentlens_session`` cookie.

The cookie is HttpOnly, SameSite=Strict, Path=/ and (in production) Secure.
The response body carries the CSRF nonce the browser must echo on later
cookie-authenticated mutations.

Enqueue a durable ROLLBACK operation idempotently and answer 202.

Authorization mirrors the target-owner rule: a principal whose
``allowed_target_ids`` excludes the changeset's target is answered with the
same 404 ``resource_not_found`` as a missing changeset, so a rollback is
never enqueued for (or its existence leaked to) an unauthorized target.
The check happens against the resolved changeset BEFORE the idempotent
execution path; a replayed same-key request re-validates it (the changeset
row is durable) and returns the pinned ``OperationAccepted``.
